messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: AtlasPay renewal: SOC 2 evidence, log-retention split & seat onramp

Hi Sara / AtlasPay procurement team —

Hope you had a good weekend. We're approaching the renewal for your account (contract ends 2026-12-15) and wanted to align on a couple of items the audit team flagged and how they affect pricing and capacity. High-level asks: 

- SOC 2 re-attestation: we can provide the standard evidence bundle (control maps, recent snapshots, SOC2 opinion).
- Log retention: your security team asked for a split retention policy (US: 90 days active + 365 days archive; EU: 365 days active) to satisfy local regulations. That will change storage/tiering assumptions.
- Capacity/seat onramp: you mentioned adding 8 Dedicated inference seats for peak batch ingestion starting Jan 2027. We'll need to reserve capacity and adjust the commit.

I've attached a draft evidence matrix and a quick cost breakout for the retention split so you can see the delta. Can you confirm: 1) whether Brightline (your auditor) needs direct read-only S3 access or just exported bundles, and 2) whether the procurement team wants a single amendment (term + retention) or separate PO for the Dedicated seats?

Next steps I propose: get auditor access requirements this week, circulate a redline of the amendment, and lock seat provisioning timeline so we can capacity-plan. Ben and Rishi — looping you for pricing/ops.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Renewal & Expansion
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-matrix-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), log-retention-cost-breakdown.csv (csv)

From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@atlaspay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@atlaspay.com>, procurement@atlaspay.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasPay renewal: SOC 2 evidence, log-retention split & seat onramp

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side after a quick sync with security and procurement: 

- Auditor access: Brightline would prefer exported evidence bundles for application controls and a scoped S3 read-only window for log snapshots (7 days during handoff). Their primary request is that we can produce an immutable snapshot of the last 12 months of auth/audit logs on demand.
- Retention split: EU business requires 365 days of active retention (they cannot rely on archive-only) due to regulatory review cycles. US team is okay with 90 days active + 365 archived if the archive is immutable and searchable.
- Procurement prefers a single contract amendment that includes: extended retention terms, pricing delta for storage, and a seat onramp schedule. They want line-item visibility in the PO.

On capacity: we expect the Dedicated seats to be used for peak batch embedding jobs (~6-8qps sustained for 3 hours/day) and occasional bulk exports. Please include burst pricing and lead time in the amendment.

Tom
Director, IT Ops
AtlasPay

--

Laura / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick notes on pricing and ops: 

- Storage delta: The proposed split (US 90/365 archive, EU 365 active) increases estimated monthly storage cost ~18% for AtlasPay's current volume (see attached csv). We can make this a line item in the amendment with a 12-month pass-through price.
- Seat reservation: For 8 Dedicated seats, ops needs a 6-week lead time for GPU pool changes if they require specific instance types; 2 weeks if generic reserved pool is fine. Recommend we offer a phased onramp: provision 4 seats on Jan 10, 2027 and the remaining 4 on Feb 7, 2027.
- Audit handoff: We can support Brightline with exported bundles and a time-boxed S3 read-only window; recommend that we require an NDA + signed request form to enable direct access.

I'll draft a pricing appendix and a ramp schedule. Rishi / Priyom — can you validate ops lead times and confirm rollback plan if capacity spike exceeds forecasts?

Ben
Senior Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasPay renewal: SOC 2 evidence, log-retention split & seat onramp

Looping back with ops details and mitigation: 

- Lead times: confirmed — generic reserved pool = 14 days, specific GPU SKU customization = 42 days. We'll plan to reserve a generic pool and leave option to migrate if AtlasPay signs earlier.
- Cost control: suggest we enable prefix-level KV caching for the batch embedding jobs to reduce token compute cost during daily runs. That will keep burst charges low and avoids overallocation of GPUs.
- Audit snapshot: ops can produce a daily immutable snapshot for the last 12 months; the S3 read-only window for Brightline can be configured for a 7-day access token and audit logs will be exported in newline-delimited JSON with checksums.

I'll prepare the ops appendix and a short runbook for the audit window; Ben, can you add the runbook link into the amendment?

Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
